memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand towards the sky so that darkness spreads over Egypt—darkness that can be felt." So Moses stretched out his hand towards the sky, and total darkness covered all Egypt for three days." - Exodus 10:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Darkness that can be felt. It is a haunting phrase. Not just the absence of light, but a heaviness pressing on people for three full days.

Egypt worshipped the sun as its chief deity, and Pharaoh was regarded as the sun god's son. God blots it out. The greatest god of Egypt simply disappears, and no one can do a thing about it.

Some of us know something of felt darkness — the heaviness of depression, the fog of grief, the season when prayer feels like speaking into a wall. It is real, and Scripture never treats it as a failure of faith. Even the psalmist wrote that darkness was his closest friend.

Hold on to this: darkness is not outside God's rule. He was Lord over Egypt's three days as surely as over its sunlight.

And remember another three-day darkness. When Christ hung on the cross, darkness covered the land (Lk 23:44-45). He entered the deepest darkness so that we would never face it alone or unredeemed.

If you are in the dark today, you are not beyond His reach.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What darkness am I carrying that I have not brought honestly to God?
2. Does it help to know Christ Himself entered darkness for me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when darkness presses in, remind me that You are still Lord over it. Hold me until the light returns. Amen.
